_meta.indication: Treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas (PN) not amenable to complete resection

pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥2 years of age with symptomatic, inoperable NF1-associated plexiform neurofibromas causing significant morbidity; GOMEKLI dosed 2 mg/m2 orally twice daily for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) by BICR, defined as complete response or partial response (≥20% reduction in PN volume) per modified REiNS criteria; secondary endpoint duration of response
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR 41% in adults (24/58; 95% CI 29, 55) and 52% in pediatric patients (29/56; 95% CI 38, 65); DoR ≥12 months in 88% (adults) and 90% (pediatric)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>25%) were rash, diarrhea, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, vomiting, and fatigue; most common Grade 3/4 laboratory abnormality (>2%) was increased creatine phosphokinase. In the pooled safety population rash occurred in 84% (31% Grade 2, 6% Grade 3). Permanent discontinuation due to an adverse reaction occurred in 22% of adult patients.
target_moa: Mirdametinib is a small molecule inhibitor of MEK1 and MEK2 (mitogen-activated protein kinases 1 and 2), upstream regulators of the ERK pathway; it inhibited MEK1 and MEK2 kinase activity with Ki values of 1.1 nM and 0.79 nM, respectively, and reduced neurofibroma growth in an NF1 mouse model

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee

summary.text: Mirdametinib received regular (traditional) approval for NF1-associated symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas based on overall response rate and duration of response from the single-arm ReNeu study. The application was a priority review NDA and had Orphan Drug (30Oct2018), Fast Track (28May2019), and Rare Pediatric Disease (24Jul2023) designations.

citations.quote: The review team recommends regular approval of mirdametinib for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas not amenable to complete surgical resection.

FDA considers ORR, supported by DOR, to be an appropriate endpoint for regular approval for this rare patient population given that their clinical meaningfulness is associated with improved clinical outcome assessment data from the ReNeu study.
